source: Minchat Shai on Gen 9:29 (his longest Genesis note — the two camps)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION, the block's headline — ויהיו כל ימי נח ("and all the days of Noah WERE," plural): the manuscript war Minchat Shai documents at length. One camp (the Jericho chumash, old manuscripts, the Ramah's seven-count Masorah): Enoch and Lamech singular, NOAH PLURAL. The other (the Hilleli, all Sepharad books, the Ezra codex, Or Torah, Minchat Kohen, the Ramah's own scroll per the Burgos sages): Noah SINGULAR, a three-member list. SNAPSHOT reads PLURAL — the Jericho camp — and its own ledger census agrees end to end: seven plural totals in the ledger plus Noah, with EXACTLY Enoch and Lamech singular — the two-singular anomaly gen_14's derivation held unexplained is the Jericho tradition's own sign (their mnemonic: the two, "until Elijah comes"). Both camps recorded; the letter locked.

ויטע ("and he planted") — the Masorah trio, ALL THREE in the Torah: God plants the garden (2:8), Noah plants the vineyard (9:20), Abraham plants the tamarisk (21:33) — "whence did he take the planting? from the Garden of Eden" (Kitzur). SNAPSHOT: exactly three tokens.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 9:21 (Masorah; Bereshit Rabbah 36; Rashi)
claim_en: אהלה ("his tent" — written with a final HE where the read form is "his") — "one of FOUR so written" (the Masorah's list: 9:21, 12:8, 13:3, 35:21 — all in Genesis): Bereshit Rabbah reads "the tent of HIS WIFE"; Rashi carries the ten-tribes hint (the northern kingdom named Oholah, exiled over wine). SNAPSHOT: the he-spelling locked.
שם וחם ויפת — the vav of ויפת ("and Japheth") with QAMATZ (the long a-vowel), "like the second one nearby" (9:23). SNAPSHOT: both qamatz.
ויגד ("and he told" — Ham's report) — the gimel with dagesh (doubling dot) and the lengthening stroke. SNAPSHOT: the dotted gimel locked.
אחרנית ("backward" — the sons' walk) — the nun with dagesh (doubling dot) "in both" occurrences. SNAPSHOT at this one: dotted nun locked.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 9:24 (Ramah — against the Mikhlol's one-yod)
claim_en: וייקץ ("and Noah AWOKE from his wine") — the Mikhlol prints one yod; Minchat Shai: "his words bewilder me, for in ALL the books two yods," and the Ramah rules it — "two yods written, ONE READ AND ONE NOT READ." SNAPSHOT: both yods in the written skeleton.
וייקץ — and its qof with SEGOL (short e-vowel), where Jacob's waking (28:16) and Pharaoh's (41:4) take patach: the Ramah distinguishes Noah's waking by its vowel. SNAPSHOT: segol.

ברוך יהוה אלהי שם ("blessed is the LORD, the God of Shem") — the Masorah: one of THREE first-stressed אלהי ("God of"), with "gods of silver" (Exod 20:23) and "the God of old" (Deut 33:27) — all three in the Torah. SNAPSHOT's accent sits on the FIRST syllable of the word — stress position read from the accent glyph's placement: a new check idiom.
